name: NGL Fine-Chem Ltd
tagline: Conservative, debt-light veterinary/human-pharma intermediate maker with a deep high-quality community track record; the FY25 margin trough has now clearly recovered (FY26 PAT +128%, Q1FY27 PAT +99%) with greenfield Phase II and regulated-market entry still ahead
business_overview: NGL Fine-Chem manufactures and exports pharmaceutical/veterinary intermediates and formulations, with capacity expansion through its Macrotech Polychem subsidiary (brownfield, now commissioned) and a Rs 210 Cr greenfield project at Tarapur (Phase I operational; Phase II commercial production expected H2 FY27). Entering regulated (US/EU) markets, expected to contribute meaningfully from FY28.

fundamentals_narrative: The cyclical margin trough that had capped conviction (gross margin 55%->46% by Feb 2025, 'washout quarter') has clearly reversed: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 36% to Rs 501 Cr and PAT more than doubled to Rs 48 Cr, and Q1FY27 continued it (revenue +34%, EBITDA margin 16.7% vs 10.5% a year earlier, PAT +99%). Management cautions that part of the Q1 lift was inventory gains on price increases and guides a steady-state 15-18% EBITDA margin. Capacity is the forward lever: the Macrotech Polychem brownfield is commissioned, and the Rs 210 Cr Tarapur greenfield (Rs ~183 Cr already spent) has Phase I operational with Phase II commercial production slipped to H2 FY27 on gas/labour delays. Regulated (US/EU) market entry is expected to contribute from FY28 with a 3-5% margin premium. Leverage stays conservative (D/E ~17.6%), promoters confirmed nil encumbrance, and the business retains the deepest, highest-quality community coverage in this batch. Valuation has partly caught up — ~39x trailing / ~25x on annualised Q1FY27.
technical_read: Not independently pulled this pass. Stock de-rated from ~Rs 3,600 to the low-Rs 1,200s through the trough and has been recovering with the earnings turn.

The FY26 / Q1FY27 recovery post-dates the posts read.

track_record.note: FY23-FY26 verifiable from the same filings. FY23 and FY26 combined >=10% revenue growth with ROCE ~16-18% -> pass. open_questions: Trailing 3y FCF conversion is modest because FY24-26 spanned a heavy capex cycle (Rs 210 Cr Tarapur + Macrotech) against trough-then-recovering EBITDA; conversion should improve as Phase II lands and capex intensity falls, but that is unproven

four_box.note: tailwind weak — China+1 in veterinary/pharma intermediates is real but the niche has recurring price competition. tam weak — global vet-API market is small; a 10x from Rs 1,861 Cr needs NGL to become a much larger regulated-market API player, a long runway. moat weak — cost/process competitiveness, not pricing power (thread confirms 'high competition, lower prices'). valuation weak — ~25x forward after the recovery move, no longer washed out.
